comments.body:
## Analysis and fixes

I reviewed the full solution for mathematical gaps and verified the quantitative results numerically (SRS-vs-stratified variance/ANOVA, SYS<=STR under convex covariance, and the IMSE Cauchy-Schwarz chain all check out).

I found and repaired **two genuinely non-rigorous spots** (both asserted without proof):

### 1. Corollary "Why grids are nearly optimal for R"
Old proof claimed the grid is "the exact minimizer on a torus by Fourier diagonalization." Numerics show the naive Fourier/continuous bound 1/c0 is NOT attained at finite n, so that argument does not establish finite-n optimality. I rewrote the corollary to prove only exact facts (each numerically verified):
(i) on the torus c_a = int K is constant, so min MSE <=> max V(P)=1^T Sigma^{-1} 1;
(ii) for the grid Sigma is circulant, 1 is an eigenvector with eigenvalue lambda0=sum_j K(j/n), giving equal optimal weights, V(G)=n/lambda0, MSE=Var(R)-n cbar^2/lambda0;
(iii) the grid is a CRITICAL configuration: gradient of V vanishes there (sum_j K'(j/n)=0 by oddness of K' + cyclic symmetry; verified ~1e-15).
Global torus-optimality is now in a separate Remark as "numerically confirmed, not proven here."

### 2. Theorem "Adaptive cannot beat the best fixed design..."
Part (a) (known-covariance Gaussian) was correct; I tightened it (condition on realized location set, pointwise bound, then expectation). Part (b) falsely claimed adaptivity "strictly reduces expected MSE relative to ANY fixed design." Restated correctly: when theta->D*(theta) is non-constant, no single fixed design is optimal for all theta, so any fixed design is strictly suboptimal at some theta, and an adaptive rule with consistent theta-hat converges to D*(theta); explicitly disclaiming any uniform strict improvement.

Updated Summary bullet (c) accordingly. All environments balance; brace check passes. No LaTeX toolchain in sandbox to compile.

These were the only places the write-up asserted more than its proof established; fixes keep all proven results and replace the two overclaims with rigorous, verified statements.
